evidence.note: claim: H.payload offers 'approve + standing window (24h)' for approve.partial even when the target is a measured baseline-red partial only a person accepts (policy.person_only_target); mechanism: _generic keys only on verb in standing_verbs; probe: test_the_standing_window_option_is_hidden_for_a_person_only_partial asserts the option is absent and passes on the fixed code
read the research-gate guidance (r-task-phase-needs-wave, r-gemini-key-load) from gate status before changing code; fixer role rules: tests-first and claim-before-edit followed

harness._generic now hides the standing-window option when policy.person_only_target(it, verb, target) holds, resolving it from the ask canon; payload threads state; both call sites (api/approvals_harness.approvals_ask, services/ask/channels._harness) pass it

chunk_findings.detail: The standing-window option is still added whenever the item cannot be resolved. `payload` sets `it = state.items.get(str(_canon_of(row).get("item", "")))` only when `state` is not `None`, and `_generic` checks `PO.person_only_target` only when `it is not None`. Therefore a person-only `approve.partial` ask whose canonical item is missing from `state.items` (or any caller that uses the new default `H.payload(row, cfg)` without passing `state`) will have `it=None`, `_generic` will return `True` if the verb/min-level checks pass, and `payload` will append `Approve {ask_id} + standing window (24h)`. For example, with `row = {"id":"A1","verb":"approve.partial","min_level":LEVEL,"canon":json.dumps({"item":"I1","target":"src/x.py"})}`, `cfg.approvals.standing_verbs` containing `"approve.partial"`, and `state=None` or `state.items` lacking `"I1"`, the returned options still include the standing-window choice—the exact choice Bdeb98fa2d1 says must be hidden for a person-only baseline-red partial.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py:payload/_generic

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test exercises `H.payload`, but the manifest says `ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py` adds `payload` as part of this change. On the pre-change tree, running `test_the_standing_window_option_is_hidden_for_a_person_only_partial` therefore fails in `_window_offered` with an `AttributeError` for the missing `H.payload` before it can assert anything about the standing-window option. That makes the test dependent on the fix’s new payload builder rather than a true regression guard for the existing ask-payload path; the old person-only `approve.partial` bug could remain in the pre-fix payload path while this test cannot demonstrate it.
